fictional_reviews.text: [Fictional review] Imagined OSRS veteran: fusing two maxed towers into a Scorching bow on wave 90 while Zulrah cycled forms felt like a real raid mechanic in TD form. The cache-baked sprites and sounds sell the fantasy completely.

[Fictional review] Made-up casual TD fan note: the board looks great and the Classic loop clicks along, but 130 waves plus Roguelite cards, relics, diaries and six skills is a lot to learn from stills alone, and the page admits balance is still WIP.

[Fictional review] Invented systems-nerd take: twelve forgeable towers, fourteen bosses with bespoke mechanics, monster affixes, seven regions and a daily seed with a scoreboard, all static-hosted with 1,700 tests? Absurd scope for a fan prototype.

how_to_play: Open https://hamilton-junior.github.io/osrs-tower-defense/ in a browser; nothing to install and no account needed.
Pick a mode (Classic or Roguelite) and a difficulty tier starting at Normal; winning unlocks the next tier up to Grandmaster.
Build towers beside the procedurally cut road on the 45x20 board; upgrade them through OSRS-gear tier ladders and fuse matching finished pairs into six forge weapons.
Kill a boss every tenth wave; after each boss pick one of seven regions to march to next, keeping towers, terrain and carved bends.
Survive to wave 130 to win the run; Endless mode keeps counting after that, and the daily challenge offers the same map and boss order per UTC day.
mechanics: Fixed 45x20 board at 1440x640 with a different procedurally cut road every run; monsters march it end to end and each leak costs one of 20 lives
130-wave run structure with a boss every tenth wave, win at wave 130, Endless beyond; seven unlockable regions change palette, native monsters and diary tasks while towers and terrain persist
Two modes: Classic (pure TD) and Roguelite (reward cards bought with gold between waves plus rule-rewriting relics from bosses)
Seven Combat-Achievement-tier difficulties from Normal to Grandmaster (up to 2.8x enemy HP, 30% less gold, five lives); wins unlock the next tier
Twelve towers: six base (Archer, Wizard, Cannon, TzHaar, Slayer, Toxic) with OSRS-gear tier ladders plus six fused weapons from adjacent finished pairs
61 monsters and 14 bosses with bespoke mechanics (Zulrah form rotation, Jad healer drain, Corporeal Beast tower siphon) plus volatile/warded monster affixes
Wizard spellbooks: single-target Elemental, crowd Ancients barrage, or Utility curses and sanctity
OSRS skills in TD roles: Slayer tasks, Prayer damage/protection burn, Herblore wave-length potions, plus Farming, Fishing and Hunter without timing or APM demands

Metagame: Collection Log, rotatable-model Bestiary, Combat Achievements, per-region Diaries, boss pets, permanent Essence Shop upgrades, daily seeded challenge with best-score board, browser-local saves plus transferable save codes

rating.reason: Closest comparators: Ashlands (55, catalog top on paper breadth with 3D engine tech but zero inspectable screenshots), Kart Royale (50, complete 3D arcade loop with polished frames but one track and thin systems), neverquest (45, deepest prior systems scope but text-UI only), and Taipo (35, fellow tower defense with one small map and three towers). OSRS Tower Defense exceeds Kart Royale and neverquest on gameplay depth and scope (12 forgeable towers, 61 monsters, 14 bosses with bespoke mechanics, affixes, spellbooks, six OSRS skills, two modes, seven difficulties, 130 waves plus Endless, seven regions, collection/achievement/diary/pet/shop metagame, daily seed, ~890 commits, 1,703 tests across 70 files) and crushes Taipo on TD scope, while its screenshots show a denser, more authentic 2D scene than Taipo's sparse map. It sits below Ashlands (55) because Ashlands claims a far more ambitious custom 3D engine and verification harness, and OSRS TD is explicitly a prototype/WIP ('nothing here is final', 3 stars, 2 forks) with no live playthrough, video, performance, balance, or late-wave verification available — source and stills alone do not prove playability, performance, or balance.

reconstructed_prompt: Build OSRS Tower Defense: a browser tower defense rebuilding Old School RuneScape with sprites and sounds baked from the real OSRS game cache. One 45x20 board with a procedurally cut road per run, 130 waves with a boss every tenth wave plus Endless, seven regions, Classic and Roguelite modes, seven Combat-Achievement difficulties, six base towers with OSRS-gear ladders fusing into six special weapons, 61 monsters and 14 bosses with bespoke mechanics and affixes, wizard spellbooks, OSRS skills (Slayer/Prayer/Herblore/Farming/Fishing/Hunter), Collection Log/Bestiary/Achievements/Diaries/pets/Essence Shop metagame, daily seeded challenge, browser-local saves with transfer codes. Next.js + React + TypeScript + Canvas 2D static export on GitHub Pages, imperative engine with pure-function tested systems.

screenshot_based_score.reason: Board frame shows a dense coherent top-down 2D scene: textured grass with trees, rocks, flowers and ruins, varied OSRS-authentic tower/enemy sprites, winding road, boss HP bar, wave banner, damage numbers, tower hotbar and full gold/lives/speed HUD — clearly the game's own runtime output and richer than Taipo (55, sparse flat map with empty water) and THORNMERE (60). Below the catalog 70s (Kart Royale, Turbo Kart Rally, Neural Sight) which show 3D lighting, depth, crowds/scenery or photographic detail that a flat canvas cannot match. Collection-log frame is real game UI with a modal overlay; start frame is a menu picker, discounted as non-gameplay. Judged from stills only; no motion, feel, or performance inferred.

screenshots.observation: Inspected 1600x900 gameplay frame: active boss wave ('Brutus 20407/21559', 'Wave 60 BOSS, 36 left') on a grass board with winding dirt road, OSRS-authentic towers and enemies, red damage numbers, green HP bars, tower hotbar mid-bottom and full HUD (speed, gold 3,902, lives 20, wave controls). Clearly the game's own runtime output; sharpest and most detailed frame.

Inspected 1600x900 game-UI frame: Collection Log modal (Monsters tab, 52/61 found, sprite grid with kill counts) over a desert-region board with winding road and bottom HUD. Real game UI, but a modal overlay rather than active combat; ranked after the pure gameplay frame.

Inspected 1600x900 menu frame: mode and difficulty picker (Classic vs Roguelite cards, Normal through NG+ Grandmaster tiers, Confirm button, 'Work in progress' note) over a torch-lit lobby. Menu/title selection, not active gameplay; discounted for graphics scoring.

source_analysis.finding: Repository is hamilton-junior/osrs-tower-defense, described as 'OSRS Tower Defense prototype', TypeScript primary language, homepage set to the playable GitHub Pages URL, 3 stars and 2 forks.

Game runs in the browser with no server; every sprite and sound is baked from the real OSRS game cache via scripts, nothing hot-linked; playable link with browser-local progress and transferable save codes.
Run structure: one 45x20 board at fixed 1440x640 with a different road every run, 20 lives, boss every tenth wave, seven regions to choose between after bosses, win at wave 130 with Endless after.

Two modes (Classic pure TD; Roguelite with gold-bought reward cards and boss-paid rule-rewriting relics) and seven Combat-Achievement difficulties up to Grandmaster (2.8x HP, 30% less gold, five lives).

Six base towers with OSRS-gear tier ladders fusing into six special weapons; 61 monsters and 14 bosses with bespoke mechanics (Zulrah forms, Jad healers, Corporeal siphon) plus Volatile/Warded affixes; wizard spellbooks; OSRS skills without timing or APM demands.
Metagame: Collection Log, rotatable-model Bestiary, Combat Achievements, per-region Diaries, boss pets, permanent Essence Shop, and a shared-seed daily challenge with best-score board.

Stack is Next.js 15.4.11 App Router + React 19 + TypeScript + Canvas 2D + Tailwind v4, static export to GitHub Pages with no backend; 1,703 Vitest tests across 70 files; imperative engine plus stateless renderer bridged by GameRoot.

Mouse/pointer play is core: tile clicks arm and spend builds, clicks pin enemy panels, pointer drives the placement ghost; keyboard is supported via an arrow-key placement cursor plus keydown/keyup handlers and hotkeys.

Viewport metadata locks touch pinch zoom and the canvas uses a touch-none class, but no on-screen joystick or documented touch controls are described; touch support is therefore unestablished rather than ruled out.
Play is single-player on one local board with browser-local saves; no multiplayer mode is documented, and the daily scoreboard only keeps each player's solo best.

Live Pages URL returns the game shell (title plus Play link) and is referenced as GAME_URL in the app source; as a JS-rendered Canvas app its full playability could not be verified from a static fetch.
No catalog entry matches this game: no existing game references this repository, playable URL, or project; the only tower-defense entry (Taipo) is a different project by a different author.
